summary: Announces the first Network Data Management meeting, to be held August 2 and 3 in Cambridge, Massachusetts, hosted by Richard Winter of the Computer Corporation of America. It gives the room, a block of hotel rooms and directions.

subtitle: An announcement and agenda for the first Network Data Management meeting.

tldr.problem: Researchers needed a forum to exchange ideas about managing and sharing data across computer networks.
tldr.mechanism: The announcement sets out a two-day meeting at CCA with presentations, informal discussion and a planning session.
tldr.outcome: The agenda covered data-sharing approaches, languages, the Data Computer and experimentation.

today: RFC 188 is a meeting announcement published in January 1971. The unit metadata lists its status as Unknown.

sections.title: Purpose and Location
sections.content:
The first Network Data Management meeting was scheduled for August 2 and 3 at CCA in Cambridge. The meeting was intended to let participants exchange ideas and develop a working data management group through paper discussions and informal sessions.

The announcement includes lodging and travel information and asks participants to review several RFCs on data management.
sections.plainLanguage: The meeting brought people together to discuss network data management and plan group work. It combined prepared talks with informal discussion.

sections.title: Monday's Agenda
sections.content:
Monday morning was to begin with an introduction and presentations on data-sharing approaches, a Unified Data Management System and a data management overview. The afternoon agenda covered data definition language, the CODASYL report, data access language and data disposition.

An informal discussion of the day's ideas was planned for Monday evening.
sections.plainLanguage: Monday's talks covered different ways to share data and languages for describing or accessing it. Participants were also scheduled to discuss the presentations informally.

sections.title: Tuesday's Agenda
sections.content: Tuesday morning was to cover the Data Computer, plans for its use and experimentation. The meeting agenda reserved Tuesday afternoon for a planning session.
sections.plainLanguage: Tuesday's program focused on the Data Computer, its possible use and experiments. The afternoon was set aside for planning next steps.
